project_name: Suncity–Karvenagar Mutha River Bridge and Approach Roads
affected_road_stretch: Suncity/Anandnagar on Sinhagad Road to Karvenagar DP Road near Dudhane Lawns; bridge crosses the Mutha River and connects directly into the Sinhagad Road network.
status_as_of_2026_08_24: Bridge opened/targeted for operation in May 2026; approach-road and connecting-road works remain relevant to the corridor.
source_notes: PMC officials reported construction began in January 2024 with a 30-month project duration. In July 2026, PMC was expediting the approach-road/land-acquisition work and a report said the flyover was ~80% complete with an intended opening within about 2.5 months. The bridge itself was targeted for opening by 26 May 2026.
use_for_demo: YES — use the approach-road/connection component as an active infrastructure constraint near the Sinhagad Road–Karvenagar end.

project_name: Pune Metro Line 4 — Kharadi to Khadakwasla
executing_agency: Maharashtra Metro Rail Corporation Limited (Maha Metro)
affected_road_stretch: Kharadi–Hadapsar–Swargate–Sinhagad Road–Dandekar Pul–Khadakwasla corridor. The current construction package covers Dandekar Pul (excluding) to Khadakwasla: 9.675 km with 8 elevated stations.
status_as_of_2026_08_24: Active procurement/construction preparation; viaduct construction tender issued in June 2026.
source_notes: The official Line 4 page states the 25.52 km Kharadi–Khadakwasla line runs along Sinhgad Road. Maha Metro's tender P2-C03/2026, dated 26 June 2026, covers viaduct and elevated-station construction from Dandekar Pul to Khadakwasla. Maha Metro's April 2026 presentation said the Line 4/4A projects were targeted for completion within four years; 13 April 2030 is therefore a derived approximate completion date, not a formally published fixed completion date.
use_for_demo: YES — strongest real project for demonstrating a utility-permit-vs-major-project conflict.

affected_road_stretch: Rajaram Bridge connecting Narveer Tanaji Malusare Road (Sinhagad Road) to Karvenagar DP Road over the Mutha River.
status_as_of_2026_08_24: Pre-feasibility / project-management-consultant stage; construction has not yet begun.
source_notes: PMC issued a 16 April 2026 tender for appointment of a project-management consultant for pre-feasibility activities for widening Rajaram Bridge to 30 m. PMC subsequently cleared the consultant appointment in August 2026. Construction timing is not yet published, so completion is intentionally left null rather than fabricated. The tender listing identifies the official source website as Maharashtra's e-procurement portal (mahatenders.gov.in), but the indexed tender record available for this research was the TenderKart snapshot of PMC tender 2026_PMCP_1295259_1.
use_for_demo: YES — excellent planned-project conflict for permits near Rajaram Bridge.

project_name: Shivane–Kharadi Riverside Road — Rajaram Bridge to Jawalkar Garden Missing Link
affected_road_stretch: 22.5 km Shivane–Kharadi east–west road; specifically the ~1.85 km Rajaram Bridge–Jawalkar Garden section in Karvenagar, of which ~1.25 km is developed and ~0.60 km remains affected by land-acquisition constraints.
status_as_of_2026_08_24: Ongoing / fragmented; PMC is actively pursuing land acquisition and completion of the missing section.
source_notes: The broader project was approved in 2011. In 2026 PMC allocated funds and intensified land acquisition for the remaining Rajaram Bridge–Jawalkar Garden section. No defensible final completion date was found, so expected_completion is left null.
use_for_demo: YES — useful for demonstrating conflict with a planned/unfinished road project adjacent to the corridor.

project_name: Sinhagad Road Drainage and Stormwater Line Repairs near Barangani Mala
affected_road_stretch: Sinhagad Road area around Barangani Mala well and nearby water/sewer infrastructure, with repairs focused on damaged drainage/stormwater lines running close to water pipelines.
status_as_of_2026_08_24: Planned/repair programme; ₹20 crore sanctioned and surveys completed, with implementation planned.
source_notes: PMC announced a ₹20 crore programme after surveying drainage infrastructure near Barangani Mala. The source does not give a defensible construction start or completion date; the start_date is therefore a programme-year marker, not a claimed physical construction start.
use_for_demo: YES — demonstrates that CorridorIQ can coordinate utility permits against a PMC-led infrastructure/repair programme, not only other NOCs.
